# Operating Core
Loaded by every agent: every line here is paid on every spawn. Keep it lean.
- Coordinator (main thread): also read [`.claude/roles/coordinator.md`](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/blob/main/.claude/roles/coordinator.md) once per session.
- Consultant / engineer / engineer-m3: your rules are in `.claude/agents/<role>.md`.
- Session paths are relative to the session directory named in `.claude/.session` (created by hook; override with env `SESSION_DIR`).

## 0. Precedence
Token minimisation governs every choice. Only these outrank it:
1. Correctness of the delivered work.
2. Mandatory deliverables and completion criteria in `TASK.md`.
3. Role boundaries (§2) and budgets (§4). They exist to minimise tokens and are never traded for convenience.

Everything else (records, reports, visuals, document formats) is produced by script or hook, or scales down with the task, unless `TASK.md` mandates it. Between correct options, take the cheaper; when unsure, the one that writes less.

<!-- TOKEN-RULES:BEGIN -->
## Token rules (all roles)
Source: `CLAUDE.md`; copied into each `.claude/agents/*.md` by [`.claude/scripts/sync-token-rules.py`](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/blob/main/.claude/scripts/sync-token-rules.py). Never edit the copies.
Output tokens are the main cost, fresh reads the next. Every rule caps one or both.
- **Context:** your prompt and brief are your whole context. Read only what they name. Before reading, check what is already captured (`STATE.md`, `context/<stream>.md`, existing outputs); never regenerate or re-read it. Missing input → return `BLOCKED`/`NEEDS`; never explore.
- **Budget:** two ceilings, `calls` (tool calls) and `out` (lines you write: files, edits, messages; lines a script generates do not count). Take the cheapest correct path; a ceiling is not a target. At either ceiling stop and return `BUDGET`.
- **Pointers, not payloads:** refer to `path:line-range` or `path#anchor`. Never copy source, specs, diffs or tool output into briefs, reports or messages.
- **Read:** clone or pull each repo once per session; read from the local checkout, never the web. Grep/Glob, line ranges, `head`/`tail`, `--stat`/`--name-only` before opening. Whole files only when marked **Full**. Never re-read an unchanged file.
- **Tool output:** summarise large output to the essentials immediately; never carry raw dumps forward. Run independent tool calls in parallel, in one turn.
- **Resume:** after a restart or compaction, resume from your `STATE.md` (agents) or `CONTEXT.md` + `ledger.py next` (coordinator); re-read sources only for what those lack.
- **Commands:** quiet flags, filters, failure-only test output; on CI failure read only the failing job's log tail. Validate cheaply (dry-run, lint, small sample) before expensive steps; on a blocking error stop and report. Allocate all identifiers/keys in one batch, at planning time.
- **Write:** targeted edits, never a whole-file rewrite for a small change. Anything repetitive, structural or derivable (skeletons, tables, indexes, file maps, reports from JSON/YAML) is generated by script. Each fact once; link elsewhere.
- **Reason:** plan once; no narration, alternatives, polish or extras; stop when acceptance is met; diagnose from the error before retrying, never blind-retry.
- **Return:** ≤5 lines per core §3. No greetings, restatements, progress or offers.
<!-- TOKEN-RULES:END -->

## 2. Roles
| Role | Model | Produces | Never |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coordinator (main thread) | session model, never switched | routing, ledger commands, user replies | read source/code/specs; design; write code, tests, scripts, specs or briefs |
| Consultant | large | decisions and engineer context: `provision.md`, specs, briefs, `context/`, answers, reviews | write code, tests, scripts or config of any size; run commands; spawn |
| Engineer | sonnet, lowest effort | all code, tests, scripts, bulk edits, generated docs, from a brief | design, guess, edit specs/briefs, spawn |
| Engineer-M3 | large | one fenced, consultant-justified, judgement-bound change | anything outside its fence; tests, docs, mechanical follow-on |

Models are pinned in each agent file and fixed at spawn; an agent keeps its model for life.

**Production rule:** only engineers produce code, tests, scripts, config or bulk edits. M3 roles exist to make engineers reliable, not to do their work. A consultant decides, from context, which class and agent receive each task.

Classes (assigned by the consultant from scope and complexity, consultant K0): **M1** well scoped, deterministic (script first) · **M2** well scoped, judgement only where the brief lists it · **M3** open judgement, design, or not yet scoped.

## 3. Communication
- Only the coordinator spawns or continues agents. Work moves through files; prompts carry paths, never content.
- Every return is ≤5 lines: line 1 status, line 2 as below, line 3 `spend: calls a/b · out c/d` (since this spawn or continue).

| Status | Meaning | Line 2 |
|---|---|---|
| `DONE` | acceptance met | acceptance result + `agents/<id>/REPORT.md` |
| `BLOCKED` | needs a decision | `agents/<id>/QUESTIONS.md` |
| `NEEDS` | work or inputs outside scope | `agents/<id>/NEEDS.md` |
| `BUDGET` | a ceiling reached | `agents/<id>/STATE.md` |

## 4. Budgets
Every spawn and continue carries both ceilings, printed by the ledger in the spawn line. Defaults live in `.claude/agents/consultant.md#budgets`; anything above a default needs a one-line `Why` in `provision.md`. Budgets rise only through re-triage, never ad hoc. `ledger.py` validates provisioning, records spend, fences writes and triggers re-triage.

## 5. Layout (session directory)
| Path | Owner | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `CONTEXT.md` | coordinator via `ledger.py decide` | link to `TASK.md`, decision log |
| `ledger.json` | `ledger.py` | task table, budgets, spend, agents |
| `provision.md` | consultant | triage table |
| `context/<stream>.md` | consultant | file map, findings |
| `context/<stream>-index.md` | engineer, by script | recon index for consultants |
| `specs/<component>.md` | consultant | implementation spec |
| `briefs/<task>.md` | consultant | engineer brief |
| `agents/<id>/` | that agent | `REPORT.md`, `QUESTIONS.md`, `NEEDS.md`, `STATE.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, `diff.patch`, artefacts |
| `prompts/` | hook | verbatim prompts + index |
| `README.md` | `ledger.py render` | session index + summary visuals |

Reference IDs: `<prefix>-<session>-<agent-id>-<NNN>`. The spawn line gives each agent its stem.


# PourSocialScore: rules and context for Claude

**Passed to every sub-agent and thread, no exceptions (the author, 2026-10-17, prompt 07 ([`temp/2026/10/17/19-14-09-Sat-ccr-ff63df4b-o4e74t/prompts/07.md`](https://github.com/racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch/blob/main/temp/2026/10/17/19-14-09-Sat-ccr-ff63df4b-o4e74t/prompts/07.md)); replaces the old token block of [`DEC-00260`](https://github.com/racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch/blob/main/documents/reference-framework/05_Detailed_Design.md#dec-00260)):** the author's prompt, the Operating Instructions at the top of this file, goes verbatim at the top of every subagent brief, `SendMessage`, `send_message`, `create_session` prompt, scheduled task prompt and workflow prompt, before the task; a thread that starts its own sub-agents passes it on the same way. It reaches them through this file, which every sub-agent and session on this repo loads, so it is never pasted by hand; a workflow script reads it from here.

## Requirements for every interaction with the AI (the author, 2026-10-10, [`DEC-00070`](https://github.com/racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch/blob/main/documents/reference-framework/05_Detailed_Design.md#dec-00070))
These apply to every prompt, reply and output in every session, whatever the task (code, a question, a build or documentation); they happen to be about documentation, but they are requirements of working with the AI, not only documentation rules.
- **Every session output is recorded in the session's temp root (2026-10-10, [`DEC-00067`](https://github.com/racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch/blob/main/documents/reference-framework/05_Detailed_Design.md#dec-00067), the author):** every output of a T2 or T3 task (Operating Instructions 2.1) is written to its scratch temp root `temp/<YYYY>/<MM>/<DD>/<hh-mm-ss>-<Ddd>-<name>/` (an `<output>/` subfolder with its own `README.md`, the prompt in `prompts/NN.md`, links in the root `README.md`), and the session's reply only links it. An output kept anywhere else (the session, the addon repo, a loose scratch folder) is not recorded. A deliverable that belongs elsewhere (a test zip, approved documentation) is hosted there as well and linked from the output's `README.md`.
- **Anything referenced always has a link (2026-10-10, [`DEC-00068`](https://github.com/racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch/blob/main/documents/reference-framework/05_Detailed_Design.md#dec-00068), the author, critical):** every reference to something the reader may open (a file, folder, section, line, key, issue, PR, commit, release, build, zip, save, repo, page, or the file a named function, event, command or saved field lives in) in anything written for the author, in any session, repository or tool (replies and summaries, documents, drafts, temp READMEs, changelogs, issues and their comments, PR bodies, comments and review replies, commit message bodies, the PR's test and in-game check lists, and subagent and workflow reports that reach the author; [`DEC-00072`](https://github.com/racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch/blob/main/documents/reference-framework/00_Decisions.md#dec-00072)) is a markdown link to it, never a bare path, number or name: scratch files `blob/main/<path>` (a section `#<anchor>`, a line `?plain=1#L<n>`), folders `tree/main/<path>`, downloads `raw/main/<path>`; addon repo files `https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/blob/<branch>/<path>`; issues, PRs, commits and releases by their GitHub URL; keys as [`DEC-00063`](https://github.com/racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch/blob/main/documents/reference-framework/05_Detailed_Design.md#dec-00063). The link text stays the short name. Not linked: commands and code in code blocks, and code names whose file is linked in the same sentence. Something that cannot be linked yet (no URL exists, for example an unpushed commit) says so beside its name. A reference found without its link is fixed in the same commit.

Three packs, read in layer order. **The baseline's rules are mandatory:** PSS overrides one only where [`docs/pss/02_RULES.md`](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/blob/main/docs/pss/02_RULES.md) section 12 (Overrides) lists it with the author's OK; any other difference is a bug, and a new difference needs a row (and the OK) first. "Baseline 02 C3" style references point into layer 1.

Release notes come from its PRs (decision 11; no build notes file). **The macros are drip-fed:** umbrella issue [#159](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/issues/159), one issue per set ([#160](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/issues/160) to [#169](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/issues/169)); the author posts macros as comments on a set's issue (first line the name, the rest the body) and asks "add the macros from [#165](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/issues/165)"; each ask is one build; the umbrella's steps and scratch `docs/latest/issues/macro-sets/` say how.
- **Graphics settings** (`/pss gfx`, Camelot): scratch `docs/latest/graphics-settings/01_DESIGN.md` (decisions 1 to 14, files, names, the rules sweep, tests, the plan) and its build record `02_BUILD_NOTES.md` (builds, patch notes, files, deviations, measured sizes, test results); read the design first; update both in every PR of the line.
- **Code map** (scratch `documents/code-map/`, component [`CMP-00015`](https://github.com/racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch/blob/main/documents/code-map/00_Appendix.md#cmp-00015), the only copy; start at its `Readme.md`: `04_High_Level_Design.md` ([`documents/code-map/04_High_Level_Design.md#hld-00013`](https://github.com/racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch/blob/main/documents/code-map/04_High_Level_Design.md#hld-00013)) the system, `05_Detailed_Design.md` ([`documents/code-map/05_Detailed_Design.md#dds-00015`](https://github.com/racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch/blob/main/documents/code-map/05_Detailed_Design.md#dds-00015)) each subsystem's API, flow and tests, `06_Architecture.md` ([`documents/code-map/06_Architecture.md#arc-00012`](https://github.com/racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch/blob/main/documents/code-map/06_Architecture.md#arc-00012)) layers and the API capability map, `09_Current_Features.md`, the generated `14_Code_Reference/`, `15_Tests/` and `16_Registries/` (every export, event, command and saved field with its callers and tests); the acceptance requirements for code are its Code Rules and Requirements ([`documents/code-map/12_User_Guides/12_02_Code_Rules_and_Requirements.md`](https://github.com/racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch/blob/main/documents/code-map/12_User_Guides/12_02_Code_Rules_and_Requirements.md))): its `Roadmaps/` ([`documents/code-map/Roadmaps/Readme.md`](https://github.com/racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch/blob/main/documents/code-map/Roadmaps/Readme.md)) folder holds the large-scale roadmaps (own bullet above); read it **first, before any source file, only** when reviewing or changing code, answering a code question or weighing a feature request; never for other work. Go to the code only for what it does not answer and to confirm what a change touches. Update it in any PR that adds, moves or removes a file, export, event, command or saved field (rerun its `gen_codemap.py` ([`documents/code-map/08_Operations/code-map-generator/gen_codemap.py`](https://github.com/racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch/blob/main/documents/code-map/08_Operations/code-map-generator/gen_codemap.py)) and refresh 04 to 06 and 09); refresh it in full at each full release. The old map (scratch `docs/latest/code-map/`) is history.

Name what they showed in the PR when it shaped the change. Never for other work.

Its appendices on scratch `docs/latest/core-uplift/` (01 core findings N1 to N48, 02 GUI G1 to G30, 03 SavedVariables, 04 upgrade helper, 05 name bugs): only the one the stage names. [`docs/pss/13_CHANGES_IN_TRAIN.md`](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/blob/main/docs/pss/13_CHANGES_IN_TRAIN.md): findings N, G, R, what shipped and what is open (refresh at each full release).

[`docs/scratch/04_USAGE.md`](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/blob/main/docs/scratch/04_USAGE.md): scratch procedures.

Baseline 02 J and B carry the rules.

## Documentation rules (one home, [`DEC-00339`](https://github.com/racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch/blob/main/documents/reference-framework/00_Decisions.md#dec-00339))
- **The Mandatory Documentation Requirements (issue [#194](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/issues/194), [`ISS-00020`](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/issues/194)) and the Reference framework (issue [#184](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/issues/184), [`ISS-00001`](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/issues/184)) apply to every document, word for word as written in** scratch `documents/reference-framework/12_User_Guides/12_02_Documentation_Rules.md`: no exceptions other than `temp/`, and none without the author's OK. Read it in full before writing or changing any document, draft, summary, report, temp README, changelog row, key or registry row.
- **This session's temp root ([`DEC-00061`](https://github.com/racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch/blob/main/documents/reference-framework/05_Detailed_Design.md#dec-00061), [`DEC-00259`](https://github.com/racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch/blob/main/documents/reference-framework/05_Detailed_Design.md#dec-00259)):** scratch `temp/<YYYY>/<MM>/<DD>/<hh-mm-ss>-<Ddd>-<name>/`, the UTC date and time of the session's first prompt, `<name>` the session's development branch without `claude/`; every output is recorded there ([`DEC-00067`](https://github.com/racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch/blob/main/documents/reference-framework/05_Detailed_Design.md#dec-00067)).
- **Startup files cite keys and paths through the reference index ([`DEC-00340`](https://github.com/racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch/blob/main/documents/reference-framework/00_Decisions.md#dec-00340)):** this file and the files it imports are written for the AI; each key resolves through scratch `documents/reference-framework/16_Registries/REGISTRY.md` (key, owner, file, title; the anchor is the key in lower case), a [``](https://github.com/racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch/blob/main/) path is in `racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch` (`blob/main/<path>`), any other path is in this repo, and `#n` is an issue or PR of this repo. The linked copy the author reads, [`docs/linked/CLAUDE.linked.md`](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/blob/main/docs/linked/CLAUDE.linked.md), is generated by `link_keys.py --render` at every docs build. Everything else written for the author keeps every link ([`DEC-00068`](https://github.com/racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch/blob/main/documents/reference-framework/05_Detailed_Design.md#dec-00068)).

## Short form
- **Current state and next steps: [`docs/pss/06_STATUS_AND_NEXT.md`](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/blob/main/docs/pss/06_STATUS_AND_NEXT.md)** (queue: scratch `docs/latest/next-steps/`). Last full release 3.7.0.114 (Addon manager, Drop Cheapest Thing, Warehouse and money; record scratch `docs/latest/release-notes/3.7.0.114.md`). Built: Spyglass phase A, 3.8.0.116, size and speed 3.8.0.117 and the pipe fix 3.8.0.118 ([PR [#238](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/issues/238)](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/pull/238)). Next: phase B, the Spyglass console, 3.8.0.121 (after the docs builds 3.8.0.119 and 3.8.0.120), then the Spyglass release 3.8.0.122 (a pre-release). Plans and the next build: scratch `Roadmaps/` ([`documents/code-map/Roadmaps/Readme.md`](https://github.com/racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch/blob/main/documents/code-map/Roadmaps/Readme.md)) (Read when the task touches the topic).
- The window is drawn in `PourSocialScore_GUI` with logic in `PourSocialScore_Libraries`; `/pss` opens it (`gui`, `ui`, `eui` aliases). Its rules: **Interface** below.
- **Versions are `X.Y.Z.B` and the build number never resets** (baseline 02 F, PSS 02 section 8): every build that gets a test zip, a stage or a fix, merged or not, takes the next number, and so does a full release; a new line counts on. Every TOC, the history section and the zip name carry it. **`versions.json`** (repo root; [`tools/versions.py`](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/blob/main/tools/versions.py)) records the latest release, every pre-release since it in order with its PR, and each past release with its pre-releases: references only, never shipped (not in a release zip, test zip or the mirror). The pipeline publishes a full release only for the version `versions.json` names the latest release, and refuses an unrecorded one. Bump with `sh tools/bump_version.sh build "Title"` (`release "Title"`, `line X.Y.Z "Title"`), then `sh tools/bump_version.sh pr <number>` once the PR is open; the rules check fails a missing or wrong PR in CI, a placeholder history bullet, and a history.txt whose top section is not the TOC version. Older names (`-devNNN`, `_N`, plain `3.3.1`) stay as they were.
- **Full releases** (checklist [`docs/pss/05_RELEASE.md`](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/blob/main/docs/pss/05_RELEASE.md), Full releases): list the PRs since the previous release (`python3 tools/versions.py prs <version>`, after `bump_version.sh release`), read each through the GitHub tools, and write **one player-facing summary of all the changes** as the release's history section (no per-build lists, no PR text). The same delivery writes on scratch `docs/latest/release-notes/<version>.md` (the summary, every change in order with build and PR, links to the technical notes; index in its `README.md`) and the release's rows in `docs/latest/summary-of-changes/SUMMARY_OF_CHANGES.md`; refreshes the code map in full (scratch `documents/code-map/`: `gen_codemap.py` rerun, its `01_Summary.md` naming the build); re-summarizes `01_HANDOVER.md`; refreshes 13; copies the PSS docs to scratch `docs/latest/pss-docs/`. Full releases are mirrored to `racetracks/Pour-Social-Score` (job `mirror`, secret `MIRROR_TOKEN`): the zip's contents committed as that repo's files and the release on that commit. Pre-releases keep their history section as notes and are not mirrored. No Claude API summary in the pipeline.
- Everything on `M` via `PourSocialScore_NS`; core fires `M.Events`; UIs write only through core setters. Tabs everywhere.
- Core holds only the chat filtering engine and the launchpad; anything not regularly active, or shared by both UIs, goes in `PourSocialScore_Libraries`, with a measured resident cost.
- No application or service logic in `PourSocialScore_GUI`. The old EllesmereUI window is in git history (tag `v3.4.0.24`).
- Every number the window shows comes from the core's counters, the same definitions as before (`check_viewquery.lua`). Logging loads only when logs are called.
- Taint and secrets (baseline 02 J, PSS 02 section 10): never write or replace Blizzard state; post-hooks and `Menu.ModifyMenu` only; every chat, unit and hook value goes through `M.PSS_IsSecret` before any compare or index; a secret line is neither filtered nor counted.
- Never change TOC Title or Notes. SavedVariables layout changes need the author's OK and a migration validated on every real save.
- **Every saved field is in the schema map** ([`PourSocialScore/PSS_Schema.lua`](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/blob/main/PourSocialScore/PSS_Schema.lua); `check_schema.lua` in the rules check and the harness). A newer version's data is never deleted: only `RETIRED` keys go, unknown fields and layouts (`v` above what this version writes) are kept, and a rule this version cannot use is kept, not applied and reported (PSS 02 section 3).
- Never write to `racetracks/PourSocialScore-EllesmereUI` (retired). Read only: `EllesmereGaming/EllesmereUI` (all rights reserved; the UI element reference, 03 section 0), `Gethe/wow-ui-source`.
- **Simulate the WoW client while you code (required; full text in 11):** drive every changed path in the harness's simulated client (`wow_stub.lua` via `run.lua`: load a save, fire the events, commands and clicks, read the real output); give changed behaviour a check that fails on `origin/main`; say in the PR what the simulation cannot show (wrapped text, combat and chat lockdown timing, taint, client art) and put that in the in-game checks. Run every test yourself before handover and report what ran and what skipped (CI is only the backstop).
- **Every feature's design and plan name its tests** (PSS 02 section 1.7): per stage, the rules check, the harness checks, the upgrade and data checks, the window compare (`tui_compare.sh`, all three looks) and the real-save run; the release stage also names every release workflow job it needs (`release.yml`, the mirror, the scratch record) and checks it at release.
- Before pushing: `sh tools/check_rules.sh` (it also runs `check_toc.sh` on every folder and the PSS-names check), `PSS_REAL_SAVES=<out dir> sh tools/harness/validate_all.sh` on the saves built from scratch (below; includes `check_tui.lua` and every tab's check; add `PSS_SAME_AS=origin/main` for a stage that must not change the saved data, `same_saves.sh`), and `tui_compare.sh` (all three looks) for any change that should not show.

## Interface: the PSS window (PourSocialScore_GUI)
The one place for the window's rules. Details (decisions, code map, lessons): [`docs/pss/09_PSS_UI_PROJECT.md`](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/blob/main/docs/pss/09_PSS_UI_PROJECT.md); look numbers: scratch `docs/latest/ui uplift/04_LOOK_SPEC.md`.

### Every element works in all three looks (the first rule)
Three looks (option `uiSkin`), listed in this order everywhere (Options, docs):
1. **Modern** (value 2, **the default**): Blizzard's 12.x Social window art.
2. **Classic** (value 0): Blizzard's classic templates; internal name "blizzard".
3. **Dark** (value 1): the EllesmereUI port's flat style.

The saved values never change (old saves keep their look). Nothing ships that works or looks right in only one or two looks.
1. **One element, three paints.** Every control, row, pane, popup, menu and tooltip is built once, with the parts each look needs, and painted by the look shown (`ns.OnPaint`; Dark parts in `widget.pssParts`). Switching the look or the font (`uiFont`) repaints in place, with no reload.
2. **Only the paint differs.** Layout, sizes, places, text, behaviour, keys (Escape, Back, Enter) and numbers are identical in all three. A look never adds, hides or moves a feature.
3. **Modern falls back to Classic** where the client has no Modern art (Camelot, or a missing atlas): check the art, never assume it. Dark falls back to its own parts when a Blizzard template is missing.
4. **Use the kit, not raw frames:** `ns.NewButton`, `ns.NewCheck`, `ns.NewEditBox` / `NewNumberBox` / `NewSearchBox`, `ns.NewPanel`, `ns.NewRows`, `ns.NewTab`, `ns.NewDropdown` / `ns.ContextMenu` (Blizzard's Menu API in Modern and Classic, our list in Dark or without the Menu API), `ns.Tip` (GameTooltip in Modern and Classic, ours in Dark), `ns.Confirm` / `ns.CopyText` / `ns.ImportText` (the window's frame art, `ns.NewFrameArt`, in Modern and Classic; the flat panel in Dark). A new kind of control is added to the kit in all three looks first, and to the kit preview ([`tools/harness/kit_page.lua`](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/blob/main/tools/harness/kit_page.lua)).
5. **Per element, check:** its Modern art, its Classic template, its Dark parts; text faded with `SetAlpha`, never colour alpha; lines and edges one physical pixel (`ns.OnePixel`, `ns.NoSnap`); the accent is the class colour (`ns.Accent()`) in every look, with no option; fonts through `ns.Font` so `uiFont` applies (LibSharedMedia only read, only when another addon loaded it); anything that must show over Blizzard frame art sits on a frame raised above its NineSlice (level about 500).
6. **Prove it in all three looks:** `sh tools/harness/tui_compare.sh` (the window step by step in Modern, Classic and Dark; "identical" for a change that should not show, only the intended lines otherwise), `check_tui.lua` (the kit in every look), and in-game checks that name each look, on Retail and Camelot.

### Titles and popups
- **Only the main window's title carries the addon's name** ("Pour Social Score"). Popup and dialog titles say what they ask ("Remove Player?", "Remove Guild?", "Remove Rule?", "Prune Players?"), never the addon name, and sit in the title bar in Modern and Classic.
- The window's popups are our own frames (no `StaticPopupDialogs` entries from the window); each registers for Escape through `ns.EscapeCloses` after its own scripts are set. One Escape closes the top popup or menu, then steps the window up one level, then closes it.
- **Core's note and party warning popups stay Blizzard StaticPopups in every look**: core never loads the GUI folder for a popup.

### The other interface rules
- **The EllesmereUI port is the reference** for layout, features and feel (tag `v3.4.0.24`); the old GUI is not authoritative. Blizzard's Social window is the reference for Modern. Copy behaviour and numbers, never EllesmereUI's code or media.
- **EllesmereUI is the reference framework for UI elements:** when building an element needs more information, add `EllesmereGaming/EllesmereUI` to the session (`add_repo`, read only) and reference it wherever possible. Rewrite to our rules (the kit, all three looks, Libraries for logic, PSS names, zero cost, J rules); never copy it verbatim, never its media. How: [`docs/pss/03_ELLESMEREUI.md`](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/blob/main/docs/pss/03_ELLESMEREUI.md) section 0.
- **Logic in `PourSocialScore_Libraries`, drawing only in `PourSocialScore_GUI`.** No state, query, validation or flow in a drawing file; UIs write through core setters (`check_layers.lua`). No `EUI` or `Ellesmere` names in new code (`check_rules.sh`).
- **Zero cost until opened:** `/pss gui` loads Libraries and the GUI folder; each tab is built on first open; core events are heard only while the window shows (`ns.Listen`); the window drops what it read and requests a GC on close.
- **Taint and secrets:** baseline 02 J and PSS 02 section 10 apply to every UI hook and every unit or chat value the window shows or acts on.
- **Saved state:** window place, last tab and new settings live in `PSS_OptionsDB` (routed `PourSocialScoreDB` UI keys); no new SavedVariables for the window. `PSS_CharDB` (the addon manager's per-character profiles up to 3.7.0.101) is read only by upgrade step 11 (3.7.0.102): they are now the owned keys `addonSetsOf`, `addonLockOf`, `addonSelOf`, `addonPickOf` in `PSS_OptionsDB`.

## Working in a Claude Code session
Style, file hosting and messages: `11_PREFERENCES.md` (call the user "the author"; files go on scratch, never in the session, replies give links).
- **Fetch fresh repos first, in every session** ([`DEC-00053`](https://github.com/racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch/blob/main/documents/reference-framework/04_High_Level_Design.md#dec-00053)): before reading anything, `git fetch origin main` (and the session branch) in the addon repo and `git pull origin main` in scratch, then `refkey.py check`; never work from a stale checkout.
- **Install `lua5.1` first, in every session:** `apt-get install -y lua5.1` (`apt-get update` first if not found). The rules check, every harness check and the real-save run need it; never skip a check because it is missing.
- Develop on the session's `claude/...` branch from the latest `origin/main`; one step per PR, based on main; never stack. **One step per session** (baseline 02 E9 to E11): build only the stage named (the next in the current plan's table unless the author names another; several stages in one build need an Overrides row), then stop.
- If `gh` is not available, use the session's GitHub tools instead of the `gh` commands in the packs.
- **Scratch is `racetracks/Pour-Social-Score_Scratch`** (branch `main`; rules in [`docs/scratch/05_RULES.md`](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/blob/main/docs/scratch/05_RULES.md)); the old `racetracks/scratch` is no longer used. Add it to the session (`add_repo`); if it cannot be added, say so and ask. **Never a PR or branch on scratch:** check out `main` and push straight to it, even when the session names a `claude/...` branch (that is for the addon repo). Pull once per session (Operating Instructions 1.1), one commit per delivery, update its `readme.md` index when a folder's newest file changes, and reply with links (`/raw/main/<path>` for downloads, `/blob/` to read, `/tree/` for a folder).
- **Scratch is the project files:** wherever the packs say "project files" or `/mnt/project-files/...`, read scratch: `SavedVariables/<version>/` (saves), `docs/latest/` (plans and docs; read it first: `docs/README.md` is the docs index, `readme.md` the repo index), `releases/` and `latest/` (zips). Each docs release is also zipped in [`docs/`](https://github.com/racetracks/PourSocialScore/tree/main/docs) (`<name>-<date>-vN.zip`) and a project or feature release keeps a history folder `docs/<project>/`. When a plan or these docs change, refresh `docs/latest/` in the same scratch commit. Status summaries go in `summary/<project>-<YYYY-MM-DD-hh-mm>.md`.
- **Real saves are never committed here** (baseline 02 D10); they live on scratch `SavedVariables/<version>/` (2.0.44, 3.0.0, 3.2.0-dev011, 3.4.0.28, 3.4.1.50). Real-save run: `sh tools/harness/build_saves.sh <scratch checkout> <out dir>` (out dir in the session scratchpad; default `/tmp/pss-baselines`), then `PSS_REAL_SAVES=<out dir> sh tools/harness/validate_all.sh`. If scratch cannot be read, say the real-save run did not happen; never claim it did.
- The clone is shallow: before `validate_all.sh`, run `git fetch --depth=2000 origin main` (its upgrade checks rebuild old versions from history; without it the "split" checks fail on 2.0.1 and 2.0.40).
- Test zips go to scratch `releases/PourSocialScore-<version>-<YYYY-MM-DD-hh-mm>.zip`, and the same commit replaces the zip in `latest/` (scratch rule 9); `sh tools/host_build.sh <scratch checkout>` does it from HEAD (`--no-commit` to add docs to the same commit); link it as `/raw/main/<path>`.
- **Update the context in every PR:** the current project's stage table (state, PR, next build), `06_STATUS_AND_NEXT.md`, `02_RULES.md` for a new rule, `11_PREFERENCES.md` for a new preference, and the scratch copies (`docs/latest/pss-docs/`, the project's folder) in the same delivery, so a fresh session starts from this file alone.
- **At each full release** re-summarize the done stages into `01_HANDOVER.md` and take them out of the plan; this file only points to plans and designs, never copies them. The author's preferences live only in `11_PREFERENCES.md`.
- Blizzard's UI source for a template or atlas question: a sparse clone of `Gethe/wow-ui-source` (for example `Interface/AddOns/Blizzard_SharedXML`, `Blizzard_SocialUI`); read only.
